newsitem.title: USA: SciClone says has FDA orphan status for CPX.
newsitem.headline: SciClone says has FDA orphan status for CPX.

text.p: SciClone Pharmaceuticals Inc said Wednesday it was notified that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted orphan drug status for SciClone's CPX as a potential treatment for cystic fibrosis. SciClone said it will start a Phase I clinical trial program.

Orphan drug designation provides a company with tax credits for clinical research expenses, eligibility for a grant program to apply for funding for clinical trials, and seven years of market exclusivity to the first sponsor who receives FDA product approval for the orphan drug in the designated indication.
SciClone is the exclusive holder of a license for CPX as a treatment for cystic fibrosis, said it expects to gain "substantially" by having this indication.
Cystic fibrosis is a genetic disease which afflicts approximately 30,000 Americans and causes recurring respiratory infections and gastrointestinal problems.
